contentSections: The most expensive mistake in a facade project usually happens before a single panel is made. It happens at the moment you transfer the advance to a company you checked for ten minutes.

A facade is not a product you pick off a shelf. It is design, engineering, fabrication and installation, wrapped into one long job on the most visible part of your building. If the company is weak at any stage, you find out when the scaffolding is already up and the money is already gone.

This guide gives you a nine point checklist for how to choose a facade company in India. Each check tells you what to ask, what a good answer sounds like, and what should make you walk away. It works whether you are building a bungalow, a retail frontage or a commercial tower.
Quick Answer: How Do You Choose a Facade Company in India?

Verify the company's registration and address, inspect real completed projects, visit the factory, get the warranty in writing, ask for engineering drawings, approve a mock-up before production, tie payments to milestones, fix the scope in a detailed quotation, and speak to past clients. If a company resists any of these, treat it as a red flag.
The nine checks, in short:

1. Verify the business
  2. Test the portfolio
  3. See the factory
  4. Read the warranty
  5. Ask for engineering
  6. Demand a mock-up
  7. Link payment to milestones
  8. Lock the scope
  9. Talk to past clients
Why Choosing the Right Facade Company Matters So Much

A facade carries three loads at once. It must look good, since it is your building's face. It must perform, since it takes sun, wind and rain every day. And it must stay attached, since a failing panel on a building is a safety problem, not a cosmetic one.

Poor decisions show up late. A coating that fades in two summers, a joint that leaks in the first monsoon or a frame that corrodes near the coast all look fine on handover day. By the time you notice, the warranty conversation has already become difficult.
Our article on the problem with cheaper cladding explains how the lowest quote often hides the highest cost.
Check 1: Verify That the Business Is Real
Start with the basics. They take ten minutes, and many people skip them.
Ask for: company or LLP registration details, GST number, PAN, registered address and the names of directors or partners.
Green flag: details are shared quickly, match public records and tally with the address on the quotation.
Red flag: only a mobile number and a social media page. A business that wants your money but not your scrutiny is not ready for a large project.
Visit the address. A real facade company has an office, and ideally an experience centre where you can see work in person.
Check 2: Test the Portfolio, Do Not Just Look at It
Anyone can copy photos. A portfolio proves nothing until you test it.
Ask for: a list of completed projects with locations, architects and approximate dates. Ask which parts they designed, fabricated and installed themselves.
Green flag: the company names architects and clients, lets you visit a completed site and connects you to the owner.
Red flag: images with no project names, mixed styles that look like different companies' work, or a refusal to share contacts.

You can also run a reverse image search on key photos and check whether the same pictures appear on other companies' websites. Browse how a real portfolio is presented in our Metaguise project gallery.
Check 3: See the Factory
This is the check that separates serious companies from intermediaries. Many "facade companies" buy panels from someone else and fit them.
Ask for: a factory visit, or a recent unedited video walk-through of the fabrication floor.
Green flag: the company shows cutting, bending, welding and coating areas, and explains how a panel moves from drawing to dispatch.
Red flag: vague statements like "our factory is in another city" with no way to see it.
We go deeper on this in our guide to how facade panels are manufactured in India, which shows what a real manufacturing process looks like.
Check 4: Read the Warranty Before You Sign
"Lifetime warranty" is the most common empty promise in this industry.
Ask for: a written warranty that states what is covered (coating, material, workmanship), for how many years, and what is excluded.

Green flag: specific terms. For example, premium coating systems from Metaguise carry warranties ranging from 15 to 30 years depending on the finish. A good company will tell you what that means in practice.
Red flag: a verbal promise, a warranty that excludes "normal weathering" without defining it, or a warranty with no named manufacturer behind it.
Also ask who backs the coating warranty: the facade company, the coating supplier, or both. Our MetaSurface finishes page explains how finishes and warranties are structured.
Check 5: Ask for Engineering, Not Just Drawings
Pretty renders are not engineering. A real facade needs calculations and detailing.
Ask for: shop drawings, fixing details, wind load considerations, expansion joint details and a note on material grades and thickness.
Green flag: the company has an in-house design and engineering team, and explains why a given thickness or sub-frame was chosen for your height and wind zone.
Red flag: "we will see on site" answers to technical questions.
Our article on how metal facade engineering works shows what questions an engineer should be able to answer.
Check 6: Demand a Mock-Up Before Production
A mock-up is a full scale sample of the facade, built before thousands of panels are made. It shows colour, joints, fixings and how the system looks in real light.
Ask for: a mock-up of at least one bay or a representative section, with your approval before production starts.
Green flag: a mock-up is a normal part of the process, with a sign-off step.
Red flag: a company that moves from a PDF to full production with no physical approval. If the colour is wrong, you will find out on the wall.
Check 7: Tie Payments to Milestones
Advance payments are normal. Unstructured payments are not.
Ask for: a payment schedule linked to defined stages, such as design approval, material procurement, dispatch, installation progress and handover.
Green flag: each payment is tied to a visible, verifiable milestone, and the invoice matches the quotation.
Red flag: pressure to pay a large share upfront, discounts that vanish if you do not pay today, or payments to personal accounts.
Take legal or financial advice on contract terms for large projects. This article is a guide, not a substitute.
Check 8: Lock the Scope in the Quotation
Many disputes come from a vague quote. A low number often means many things are left out.

Ask for: a line item quotation that states panel type, thickness, finish, sub-frame, fixings, sealants, scaffolding or access equipment, transport, installation, taxes and any lighting or glazing interfaces.
Green flag: a detailed quote with clear inclusions and exclusions, and a way to compare it line by line with other bidders.
Red flag: one lump sum and "everything included".

As a reference point, Metaguise installed systems typically fall between INR 800 and INR 2,500 per sq ft depending on system and complexity. Use that range to sanity check bids, and see our metal facade cost guide for what drives the number.
Check 9: Talk to Past Clients and Read Reviews Carefully
Facade company reviews are useful if you read them like an investigator.
Ask for: two or three past clients you can call, ideally from projects completed at least a year ago.
Green flag: clients mention how the team handled problems, not just how the facade looks.
Red flag: only five-star reviews posted in a single week, or reviews that never mention any detail of the work.
Ask past clients three things. Was the project on time? Did the final look match the approved sample? What happened when something needed fixing?

Facade Company vs Architect vs Contractor: Who Should You Hire?

Many first time clients confuse these roles. An architect designs the building. A facade designer or consultant develops the skin. A contractor or manufacturer builds and installs it. Some companies, including Metaguise, combine design, engineering, fabrication and installation, which reduces handovers and finger-pointing.
If you are unsure which route fits your project, read our guides on facade contractor versus facade designer and facade company versus architect.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I choose the best facade company in India?
Verify registration, inspect completed projects, visit the factory, read the warranty, check engineering, approve a mock-up, link payments to milestones, lock the scope and speak to past clients. Choose on proof, not promises.

How much advance should I pay a facade company?
There is no single figure. Advances should be linked to defined stages such as design approval and material procurement, with later payments tied to dispatch, installation and handover. Seek legal or financial advice for large contracts.

What is a red flag when hiring a facade contractor?
Pressure to pay quickly, no factory access, no written warranty, a lump-sum quote and a portfolio with no named projects are the most common warning signs.

Should I choose the cheapest facade quote?
Not automatically. Compare line by line. A cheaper quote may use thinner sheet, weaker coatings or leave out scaffolding and sealants, and the real cost shows up later.

Is a facade manufacturer better than a dealer?
Manufacturers control design, quality and timelines, which helps accountability. Dealers can be fine for simple products, but custom facades usually need a company that fabricates and installs its own work.

Do I need a mock-up for a small project?
Yes, even a small one. A sample panel or small section lets you check colour, finish and joint lines under real light before you commit to full production.
